headline: Twenty public namespaces that had no documentation now have pages, and the report that was supposed to find them no longer drops the ones it cannot place
summary:
`b.createApp` had no page. Neither did `b.objectStore`, `b.localDb`, `b.security`, `b.staticServe` or the whole `b.vault*` and `b.backup*` families: twenty namespaces in all, carrying seventy-one functions an operator can call and could not read about.

They were invisible because the tool that reports undocumented namespaces located each one by guessing a filename from the namespace, tried three spellings, and dropped the namespace when none of them existed. Every namespace implemented in a subdirectory therefore left the report, and the run printed that every function-bearing namespace was documented.

All twenty are documented now, each function with its signature, its options, what it refuses and why, and the version it shipped in. The resolver reads the export map in `index.js` instead of guessing, so it answers with the file that actually implements a namespace, including when the namespace is re-exported through a barrel. A namespace it still cannot place is reported with no file rather than dropped.

The report is also a gate now. It runs in the framework's own test suite and fails when a public function-bearing namespace carries no documentation, so the next one cannot arrive unnoticed.

items.title: Twenty namespaces have documentation pages
items.body: `b.createApp`, `b.objectStore`, `b.localDb`, `b.security`, `b.staticServe`, `b.safeEnv`, `b.safeJsonPath`, `b.mtlsEngine`, `b.fda21cfr11`, `b.tcpa10dlc`, `b.gdpr.ropa`, `b.nis2.report`, `b.incident.report`, `b.vaultWrap`, `b.vaultRotate`, `b.vaultPassphraseOps`, `b.vaultPassphraseSource`, `b.backupCrypto`, `b.backupManifest` and `b.backupBundle` each have a page, and each of their functions a signature, its options with defaults, the codes it raises and a worked example. Among them: that `b.createApp` installs nine middlewares without being asked and leaves `cors` and `rateLimit` for a deployment to configure; that `b.localDb.thin` fixes five pragmas and refuses a config naming any of them; that a backup's per-file subkey is bound to the file's path, so a blob moved inside a bundle stops decrypting; and that `b.mtlsEngine` picks its signature algorithm by generating a key and signing a certificate with it rather than by reading a capability flag, while the separate `canVerifyInTls` is what answers the handshake question.

items.title: A vault rotation's verification bounds reach the verification
items.body:
`b.vaultRotate.rotate` accepts `sampleMin` and `samplePercent` and did not pass either to the verification it runs over the staged copy, so an operator asking for a wider sample received the default five rows or one percent per table while believing the staged rotation had been checked more closely. Both are forwarded now. `tables` is not: it narrows what the rotation re-seals, and scoping the verification to the same subset would stop it reading the tables the rotation skipped, which is the one case that loses data at cutover. A sealed row left under the retired keypair still refuses the rotation with `vault-rotate/verify-failed`.

Both bounds are also checked before the staging directory is created. A `sampleMin` of `0` was refused after the directory existed, so the corrected retry then died on `vault-rotate/staging-exists` and the operator had to clear the directory by hand first.

items.title: A certificate's DNS subject alternative names are validated
items.body:
`b.mtlsEngine.signClientCert` and `b.mtlsEngine.packageP12` treated every `sans` entry that was not recognized as an IP address as a DNS name and wrote it into the certificate, so `"not a host !!!"` produced a certificate carrying an identity no peer can match, failing later at the handshake where the cause is hard to find. Only a value explicitly prefixed `IP:` was ever refused.

A DNS name is now checked before issuance: 1 to 253 octets, in labels of 1 to 63 letters, digits, `-` or `_`, each label starting and ending with a letter, digit or `_`, with an optional single leading `*` label. Anything else raises `mtls-engine/bad-san` naming the value. An entry that is not a string is refused too: a `null` or a port number left by a configuration placeholder was coerced and became the DNS name `"null"` or `"8443"`, both of which are valid labels. For `usage` `server` or `both` with no `sans`, the common name becomes the one DNS name and is held to the same rule, so a common name that survives normalization but cannot be a hostname, such as one made only of dots, is refused instead of issued.

A call that was issuing a usable certificate is unaffected. A call that was issuing an unusable one now raises. Underscores are accepted, since internal certificate authorities use them.

items.title: A NIS2 stage filed while the CSIRT endpoint was down can be submitted again
items.body:
`b.nis2.report` records a stage against the directive's deadline and then POSTs the envelope, so a filing lands on time even when the CSIRT endpoint is unreachable. The call reported that as `submitted: false`, but the stage was filed and calling it again raised `incident-report/stage-already-filed`, leaving the operator with a record saying the stage was filed and no way to send it.

`resubmit(incidentId, stage)` re-POSTs the envelope for an already-filed stage and leaves the deadline record untouched; `stage` is `early-warning`, `notification` or `final`. It sends the fields the stage was filed with, so the retry carries the same report the first attempt did, and a third argument replaces them for a report corrected in the meantime. A stage outside those three raises `nis2-report/bad-stage`, an unknown incident `nis2-report/unknown-incident`, and a stage not yet filed `nis2-report/stage-not-filed`.

items.title: A RoPA activity cannot be updated into an invalid one
items.body: `b.gdpr.ropa`'s `update` validated only a changed `legalBasis`, so a patch clearing `name`, `purposes` or `dataCategories` was applied and the register exported an activity missing a field Article 30 §1 requires. `update` now validates the merged record, raising `gdpr-ropa/missing-field` or `gdpr-ropa/bad-legal-basis` and leaving the stored activity alone.

items.title: A truncated backup ciphertext is refused before the key derivation
items.body: `b.backupCrypto.decryptWithKey` and `b.backupCrypto.decryptWithPassphrase` refused a buffer only at or below the 24-byte nonce, so a value of 25 to 39 bytes cleared the check, cost a full Argon2id derivation, and failed as `backup-crypto/decrypt-failed`. A sealed value needs the nonce and the 16-byte Poly1305 tag, so anything under 40 bytes now raises `backup-crypto/bad-input` first. `b.backupCrypto.TAG_BYTES` and `b.backupCrypto.MIN_SEALED_BYTES` are exported alongside `NONCE_BYTES`.

items.title: A vault passphrase from the environment has its trailing newline trimmed
items.body: `b.vaultPassphraseSource.fromFile` trimmed trailing CR and LF bytes and `fromEnv` did not, so a passphrase handed over by a mechanism that keeps the final newline, such as a shell heredoc or a file piped into a variable, opened a vault from the file source and failed from the environment source. `fromEnv` trims the same bytes now, and a value that is nothing but newlines is refused rather than read as an empty passphrase. An interior newline is still part of the passphrase.

items.title: The wrapping-key salt bound is enforced where the key is derived
items.body: The sealed-file format accepts a salt of 8 to 64 bytes, and `b.vaultWrap.buildHeader` enforced that while `b.vaultWrap.deriveWrappingKey` did not. A direct caller could derive a wrapping key under a 65-byte salt, which `buildHeader` would then refuse to record, and a salt shorter than 8 bytes surfaced as a native `ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE` from Argon2 rather than the format's own refusal. Both now raise `vault-wrap/bad-salt`, from one check that `buildHeader` shares.

items.title: A vault rotation's remaining bounds are checked before it claims the staging directory
items.body:
`rowBatchSize` was read without validation and reached the SQLite `LIMIT` bind only after the staging directory had been created and filled, so a non-integer value failed partway through and the corrected retry then died on `vault-rotate/staging-exists`. It is validated with `sampleMin` and `samplePercent`, before anything is written.

`tables` and `infraColumns` are also checked, in `rotate`, `verify` and `validateSchemaMatch` alike. A value that is not an array of names was silently ignored, so an operator who wrote `infraColumns: "audit_log"` instead of a list received drift errors on the column they meant to allowlist and no way to turn them off. Each now raises `vault-rotate/bad-opt`.

items.title: An object store built without a config refuses with a code
items.body: `b.objectStore.buildBackend()` called with no config threw a bare `Error`, so a caller catching by code could not catch it, while the same mistake against `b.objectStore.bucketOps.create()` raised `objectstore/bad-opt`. Both now raise `objectstore/bad-opt`. The message is unchanged in substance and the error still extends `Error`, so a `catch` that does not inspect the code behaves as before. `protocol` itself remains required: omitting it raises `protocol-dispatcher/missing-protocol` rather than selecting a backend nobody named.

items.title: The undocumented-namespace report no longer drops what it cannot locate
items.body: `find-missing-pages` resolved a namespace to a file by trying `lib/<namespace>.js`, its kebab-case spelling, and `lib/<namespace>/index.js`, and returned early when none existed. The namespace left the report with it, so twenty undocumented namespaces read as documented and the run reported that every one was covered. It now resolves the namespace through the export map in `index.js`, which answers with the implementing file whether the namespace sits in a subdirectory, is re-exported through a barrel, or is wrapped in an object literal, and it falls back to the filename conventions after that. A namespace that still cannot be placed is reported with no file rather than skipped.

items.title: The vendored Public Suffix List is refreshed to the 2026-10-07 snapshot
items.body: `lib/vendor/public-suffix-list.dat` carries the list published at `2026-10-07_07-28-19_UTC`, commit `3929462652695bad04f0a27afb600974014a3c8b`, re-signed and re-hashed in `lib/vendor/MANIFEST.json`. Upstream replaced twenty-seven explicit `replit.dev` entries with `*.replit.dev` and `*.teams.replit.dev`, so a registrable-domain lookup under `replit.dev` now resolves any subdomain rather than only the named ones. Everything that reads the list sees the change: `b.guardDomain`, cookie-domain checks and the public-suffix lookups in the request path.

items.title: The vendored PKI bundle is refreshed to 0.8.59
items.body: `lib/vendor/blamejs-pki.cjs` carries `@blamejs/pki` 0.8.59, with `lib/vendor/MANIFEST.json` re-hashed to match. The framework still ships zero npm runtime dependencies; this is the bundled copy the X.509, ASN.1/DER and CMS paths read.

items.title: An undocumented public namespace fails the test suite
items.body: The undocumented-namespace report ran only when someone invoked it and always exited zero. It is now asserted in the framework's own suite, which fails naming each public function-bearing namespace that carries no documentation, together with the file to put it in. The resolver is asserted separately against the namespaces whose files the old guess could not derive, so the mapping is held even while nothing is undocumented.
